related_resources.reason: Chapters 2, 3, 6, 7, and 9 cover major/minor scales, triads, cadences, and harmonic function.
Introduces functional harmonic syntax and voice-leading as distinct musical dimensions.
Checks the C-major collection and construction of degree-based chords.
Shows root, third, fifth, and inversion vocabulary used in the four-bar sketch.
Adds context for why harmonic descriptions depend on genre and expectation.

description: Addresses topics from the lecture, including "A scale is a collection; a key is a relationship"; "A chord is a set of sounding relationships"; and "Why the fifth chord often points home".
